analysis.title: EU Payments - Key Takeaways from Our TMT Conference
key_insights: Investors at the conference were broadly cautious on European payments, citing rising competition, a higher cost of growth and unproven growth in new products and markets.

Value-added services are the next growth leg. Adyen is adding Talon.One (loyalty), Orb (billing) and capital, Wise is moving into SMB workflows, and Kaspi is expanding into in-store grocery. MS sees this as a response to take-rate pressure and demand for one-stop solutions.
Cost of growth is rising, mainly through engineer hiring and some marketing. MS thinks winners will turn higher spend into above-market growth, which should support valuations.
Wise treats costs and price cuts as investments, with marketing held to 15-20 month paybacks and a 20% IRR hurdle. It signalled at 1H FY27 results that cost growth should soften.
Adyen is hiring in engineering and go-to-market to sustain about 20% growth, and says higher margins would be easy to reach if it chose to.
Pricing pressure is rising as more players enter. MS expects it to be offset by larger addressable markets through VAS and new revenue pools.
Wise is a price maker, with self-directed cuts funded by efficiency taking take rate to 49bp from 52bp and Platform pricing around 40bp.
Adyen faces processing pressure under tiered pricing but Q3 volume grew 30%, and it aims to lift take rate through loyalty, billing and fraud tools.
Kaspi payments pricing should stay stable at 95bp+, supported by its dominant fintech and marketplace position in Kazakhstan.

AI already drives efficiency at Wise (treasury ML kept working capital flat at about $250m despite fourfold volume growth, AI agents handle about 45% of chats), Adyen and Kaspi. MS sees it as margin support for now, with bigger product upside such as agentic commerce still ahead.
Adyen is ready for agentic commerce even though volumes remain slow, and token and model costs offset part of its engineering productivity savings. Kaspi launched its Kasper shopping agent.
Ratings: Adyen Overweight with PT €1,250 against €836.4 price (comp sheet). Wise Equal-weight with PT 9.9 GBP / $13. Industry view In-Line.
EU payments mean forward P/E is 19.5x 2026e, 16.1x 2027e, 13.1x 2028e (market-cap weighted), and the group is down 23.6% YTD (mean). Adyen is down 36.5% YTD.

market_movers.rationale: Medium-term topline ambition reiterated with no early 2027 guide. VAS products (Talon.One, Orb, capital) add revenue pools and Q3 volume grew 30%.
New Platform customer win and US regulatory progress, but cost of growth and take-rate cuts to 49bp are being absorbed.

sector_views.rationale: Industry View In-Line. Investors are cautious on competition and cost of growth, while MS expects VAS and larger addressable markets to offset pricing pressure.

earnings_insights: Wise 1H FY27 results were a 3% consensus miss per MS prior note (13 Nov 2026), with Platform wins and Belgian resolution seen as strategic positives.
Adyen Q3 2026 volume grew 30%. A prior note flagged a downgrade to EBITDA guidance (28 Oct 2026).
Kaspi GMV guidance reset disappointed while the EBITDA target was unchanged (9 Nov 2026).
MS EPS estimates (comp sheet): Adyen 2026e 38.06, 2027e 46.98, 2028e 59.03. Wise (WSE-US) 2026e 0.54, 2027e 0.64, 2028e 0.76. Adjusted EPS, MS estimates for covered names.
risk_factors: Adyen downside: slow new merchant wins, penetration ceiling at existing merchants, US/APAC expansion lagging, online payments commoditising, prolonged leadership transition.
Wise downside: regulatory, licence and FX exposure risk.
Rising pricing competition and take-rate pressure.
Higher cost of growth through engineer hiring, with token and model costs offsetting AI savings.
Unproven growth in new products and markets.
vol_and_positioning: Investor sentiment at the conference was broadly cautious on payments.
